text:
Leah J: hey team, just unboxed my company Mac (M3 Air) and ran through the quickstart. The profile pushed fine but the VPN installer is failing — macOS prompts me to allow a kernel extension for 'WireGuardVPN' and the installer exits. Also seeing a keychain prompt asking for a SCEP certificate which never appeared. @Ryan (IT) any ideas?
Ryan (IT): hi Leah, can you paste the installer error and run a couple quick checks? system extensions on Apple Silicon can be finicky.
Leah J: here's the install log tail and the profiles list I ran.
Installer error: "Installation failed: required kernel extension not permitted by system policy"
Command: profiles -P
--
profiles:
  - Profile: com.redwood.device.base
    Status: Installed
  - Profile: com.redwood.vpn.network
    Status: Pending - User Approval Required

systemextensionsctl list
something like:
com.apple.networking.extension: 0 extensions
com.apple.driver.some: 0 extensions

Leah J: also when I try to open Keychain Access I don't see the company cert under "System" -> "Certificates".
Ryan (IT): ok that confirms the VPN network extension/profile is waiting for user approval. On Apple Silicon we shouldn't be asking new hires to grant kernel extensions directly — security wants that staged via MDM or we use the network extension variant. Don't grant full admin just yet. I'll try to push the network extension whitelist and SCEP cert from MDM. Can you hold tight and avoid granting any allow dialogs?
Leah J: sure — I clicked "Allow" in Security & Privacy for a different app earlier, but I didn't approve anything for WireGuard.
IT Helpdesk: created ticket #INC-79421 for Leah J. Assigned to Ryan (IT) and mdm squad. Please reference this thread. :ticket:
mdm-bot: Scheduling a targeted push: will attempt to deliver com.redwood.vpn.network profile and SCEP cert to device serial ******** in ~10 minutes. If the device is offline, the push will retry.
Ryan (IT): if the MDM push succeeds you'll get a desktop notification to approve the profile; once the profile is installed the installer should succeed without any kernel prompts. If it fails we'll collect a systemdiagnose and escalate to mgmt.
Leah J: thanks — I'll keep the laptop open and connected to Wi‑Fi. Anything I should run or share if it still fails?
Ryan (IT): if it still fails, run these two commands and paste output:
profiles -P
systemextensionsctl list
Also copy any output from Console.app filtered to "wireguard" or "com.redwood.vpn".
Sophia (Security): quick note — Security prefers we avoid temporary admin elevation for new hires. We can approve a specific network extension via MDM. If the extension actually requires kernel-level kexts, we need to sign and notarize and push out via an enterprise-signed package; don't escalate to org admin yet.
mdm-bot: Push successful. com.redwood.vpn.network status: Delivered -> Installing -> Installed. SCEP cert delivered to system keychain.
Leah J: I got the "Profile Installed" popup and now the VPN installer completed! No kernel prompts. Yay :tada:
Ryan (IT): awesome. Can you confirm you can connect and see internal docs?
Leah J: connected, internal wiki loads, and dev VPN routes are there. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.
IT Helpdesk: closing ticket #INC-79421 as resolved. If any follow-up needed, reopen and tag @Ryan (IT). :white_check_mark:
